points: The people of Anasos are out to kill Yirmiyahu. He asks the age-old question, but per the Malbim, not "tzaddik v'ra lo," why good people suffer.
Why not? Because no one can say he is living up to his full potential, so we can't judge why a good person suffers. His question is why the wicked succeed and live in peace.
Seeing the wicked fall is a taste of the end of days. Watching Hamas, Hezbollah and Iran fall, we are living through incredible times.
Hashem answers: it's not just Anasos; even your own family, the Kohanim in Yerushalayim, are against you. A navi is also a test: can we listen to rebuke, even if we're not ready to change yet?
The Malbim: the purpose of exile is to teach the nations. If they learn from us to fear Hashem and be moral, they will be saved along with us.
